segments.text: Good evening. This is Akash Vani and I am Valsa Williams with the news at 9.
The headlines
Supreme Court appointed panel launches portal for complaints on July violence at Jantar Mantar
and other places. Center seeks reports from Punjab government over killings of anti-drug
activists amid narcotics linked allegations and law and order concerns.
Space Minister Dr. G. Tindra Singh says India's space economy is likely to reach 40-45 billion
US dollars in 7-8 years.
Ten people killed in a fire at a seaside resort in Cox's Bazaar district of Bangladesh.
In sports, India bags gold and silver in junior men's one-lap road race at World
Pujari wins silver at under-23 wrestling world championship in Las Vegas.
The High-Powered Inquiry Committee, HPEC, constituted by the Supreme Court to inquire
into all aspects of the incidents relating to violence at Jantar Mantar in Delhi and
at places outside Delhi during the month of July this year, has launched a portal for
submitting complaints and representations. The portal HPEC.NIC.IN has been launched for
the convenience of the affected people, including the affected police personnel.
The Ministry of Home Affairs said the HPEC shall examine all issues enumerated in the
Supreme Court's order. The Ministry added that priority will be given to matters pertaining
to the use of pellet guns, targeted violence and harassment of female protesters, and
excessive violence and destruction of property, occasioned on either side, a report.
The ministry said that the HPEC portal is designed in such a manner as to enable due
protection to vulnerable witnesses and also to keep the identities confidential and un-disclosed
if so wished by the affected persons. The affected persons and other stakeholders are
encouraged to access the portal and upload their complaints and representation making
use of the format as applicable.
Those who wish to submit the complaint, representation and other relevant material physically can
do so at the office of HPEC at Siksha Sadan New Delhi between 2 pm and 4 pm on all working
days.
Submission can also be sent by post at the Avog address or by the email at hpec2026.inquiryatnic.in.
The ministry also said that any person who wants to provide information or suggestion
relation related to the issue referred to the HPC may also do so through the portal.
The Ministry of Home Affairs has written letters to the Punjab government seeking detailed reports
on two killings and the suicide of a man amid allegations linked to narcotics and concerns
over their potential law and order implications in the state. Sources said, the ministry
has written three separate letters to the state government in this regard. We have
more from our correspondent.
The Home Ministry has sought factual and detailed reports from the Punjab government on the recent
murder of the anti-drugs crusader Parvinder Singh Chhota by a chemist in Mansa district.
Reports have also been asked for in the incidents of attack on three individuals allegedly linked
to their objections to sale of narcotics in a village of Borodistic Gurdaspur and
suicide of the father of a youth struggling with substance dependence in Senghru district.
The ministry has asked Punjab government to share a detailed report in view of the potential
law and order implications in the border state.
Rajesh Bali, Akashwani News, Jalandhar.
Meanwhile, former Punjab BAEJP President Sunil Jharkhar has written to Union Home Minister
Mithra seeking investigations by the National Investigation Agency into alleged drug operations
being run from prisons in Punjab.
Mr. Jharkhar also demanded a probe by the enforcement directorate into the black
money linked to the drug trade in the state. The Supreme Court has called for
stronger technological and regulatory measures to detect and remove child
sexual exploitation and abuse material from the internet. A bench of justices
J. B. Pardiwala and K. V. Chandran directed the creation of a comprehensive
of national database to identify and remove such content across social media platforms.
This is Aakashwani giving you the news.
Stay connected with AIR News.
Follow us on X at AIR News Alerts and visit newsaunair.gov.in for the latest updates.
Welcome back here with us on the news at 9.
Minister of State for Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh has said India's
space economy currently valued at around $9 billion is expected to reach
$40 to $45 billion over the next seven to eight years. He said this during a
media roundtable on space sovereignty and new economy organized by Bloomberg
new economy forum in New Delhi. He stressed that greater domestic and
international investment, faster regulatory approvals and sustainable business models would
be essential to scaling up Indian enterprises and expanding their presence in global markets.
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Bhupinder Yadav, today held
a meeting with startups and innovation companies working on air pollution mitigation in New
Delhi. The meeting was focused on developing practical, scalable and technology-driven
solutions to address the air pollution challenge in Delhi and adjoining national capital region.
Addressing the meeting Mr Yadav highlighted that the interaction with startups is a novel
proactive initiative aimed at bridging the gap between policymakers and technology innovators.
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, FSSAI, has published a draft amendment
to the food safety and standards foods for infant nutrition regulations 2020
proposing to prohibit the addition of sucrose and fructose in food products
intended for infants up to six months of age. FSSAI has also notified draft
amendments proposing maximum residue limits MRLs for two pesticides
Acetamide prid and imidacloprid in tea.
The draft Food Safety and Standards Contaminants, Toxins and Residues Amendment Regulations
2026 proposed MRLs of 20 milligram per kilogram for acetamide prid and 50 milligram per kilogram
for imidacloprid in tea.
Agriculture and Farmers' Well Feminist Shivraj Singh Chauhan today virtually reviewed
the preparations for the upcoming Kate Vajau Abhiyan.
The campaign will be conducted from the 22nd of this month to the 30th of next month.
During the meeting, Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers, welfare, Bhagirath
Chaudhry and Agriculture Ministers from Mathipradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, Gujarat, Uttarakhand,
Rajasthan, Assam, Haryana, Jammu and Kashmir, Bihar and Maharashtra also participated
in the meeting.
In Gujarat, five workers were killed and five others injured following a powerful reactor
explosion and subsequent toxic gas leak at a chemical manufacturing factory in Barooch
District.
The incident occurred late last night at Sinzil Farmer Chem, a unit located in the
Sekha GIDC area of Vagrataluka during a hydrogenation process.
The blast also caused a leak of a methylene dichloride gas.
The company has been given a closure notice by the authorities.
Along with this, a case of accidental death has been registered at Vagra Police Station in Bharuch.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service,
a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva
and a relentless commitment that continues.
Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan,
vision, the government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a vikasit
barat by 2047.
Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives.
Today in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated
into action through initiatives like Jan Vishwas Act.
For many years, several laws in India treated even small procedural mistakes as criminal
offenses, and many of these provisions came from older regulatory systems.
Recognizing the need to make laws more balanced and practical, the Narendra Modi government
began a process of reviewing such provisions.
An important step in this direction was the Jan Viswas Amendment of Provisions Act 2023,
which removed criminal penalties for a number of minor offenses across several central
laws.
The government continued this reform by introducing the Jan Viswas Amendment of Provisions
Bill 2026, which was passed in parliament in April this year.
In his address on Independence Day last year, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that his
government has abolished more than 40,000 unnecessary compliances and also scrapped over 1,500
absolute laws.
Addressing the press conference after the bill was passed, Commerce and Industry Minister
Piyush Goyal said that this legislation is an important milestone in the country's journey
towards Vixit Bharat 2047.
It demonstrates the trust Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his government have on the common
man because all of these 1000 sections were a source of uncertainty but a source of harassment.
We have removed all of that.
The John Viswas Act represents a major step towards modernizing India's regulatory framework
and aligning it with globally accepted principles of poor proportionate and risk-based regulation.
Anand Kumar, Akash Mani News, Delhi.
You are listening to news at 9 on Akash Mani.
Want more news? Follow us on X at AIR news alerts and subscribe to news on air official
on YouTube.
Welcome back. In Bangladesh, 10 people including 6 of our family were killed and several injured
in a fire at a seaside resort in Cox's Bazar district this morning. Local officials said
the fire broke out at Uptubresto and Resort in Ukhya, completely gutting the three-story
wooden structure.
In view of the prevailing situation in the West Asia region, Air India and Air India Express
have temporarily suspended flights to and from Jadda, Riyadh and Dhammam until the 24th
of this month.
The airline said passengers holding confirmed Air India or Air India Express bookings issued
on or before the 15th of this month, with travel dates between the 9th and 25th of
October are eligible for a one-time complementary date change on their respective airline up
to the 10th of next month.
The Indian Embassy in Bucharest today said all nine Indian seafarers aboard chemical
tanker Yara J. are safe, and the vessel has reached Romania's port of Constanta.
Indian Ambassador to Romania Manoj Mohapatra confirmed the development after speaking
with Romanian authorities and the vessel's security officer.
Meanwhile, three Indian nationals rescued from commercial vessel MV Royad Mamadov, following
an attack in the Black Sea on the 6th of this month, have left Romania for India.
In skating, India's 16-year-old speed skater Anirudh Dhan Vinod won gold in the junior
men's one-lap road race at the World Skate Games 2026 in Asuncion, Paraguay, clocking
30.394 seconds. His compatriot Lohnath Arun Prasad secured silver in the event. The margin
between the two skaters was just 0.025 seconds. India's Amrita Pujari has won a silver medal
in the women's 72kg category at the under-23 world wrestling championships at Las Vegas
in the United States today. She lost to Ukraine's Irina Zablotska 0.6 in the gold
medal bout to finish second. In men's cricket, West Indies won the toss and elected a field
against India in the series deciding 5th T20 International at M. Janiswami Stadium in Bengaluru.
The toss was delayed due to rain and the match has now been reduced to 9 overs game.
And now before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.
Supreme Court appointed panel launches portal for complaints on July violence at Jantar
and other places. Center seeks reports from Punjab government over killings of anti-drug
activists amid narcotics-linked allegations and law-and-order concerns.
Space Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh says India's space economy is likely to reach 40 to 45
billion US dollars in 7 to 8 years. Ten people killed in a fire at a seaside resort
in Fox's Bazaar district of Bangladesh.
In sports, India backs gold and silver in junior men's one-lap road race at World
Skate Games in Paraguay and Amrita Pujadi wins silver at under-23 wrestling world
championship in Las Vegas.
That is all in the news at 9, good night.
